bihar_raw_news.title: India's scheme for rare earth magnet production gains broad industry participation: Report
bihar_raw_news.content: International 03 Sep, 2026 India's scheme for rare earth magnet production gains broad industry participation: Report Business To Business, New Delhi, 03 September 2026: India has received 20 bids to build integrated rare‑earth permanent magnet manufacturing facilities and the government aims to create an integrated chain stretching from NdPr oxide to finished magnets, a new report has said. The report from Times Kuwait highlighted that India’s broader critical-mineral strategy increasingly focuses on value addition, processing and manufacturing rather than stopping at the extraction stage. The warm response by bidders to the initiative has given fresh momentum to a policy effort that goes beyond securing a raw material to forming industrial capacity necessary to convert India’s rare-earth resources into high-value products for the country's fastest-growing sector, the report said. India's $7.74 billion rare‑earth permanent scheme aims to create 6,000 metric tonnes per annum of integrated REPM manufacturing capacity in India. Ministry of Heavy Industries invited proposals on March 20, 2026 and opened technical bids on August 13, 2026, as companies including Larsen & Toubro, Coal India, ReNew, Attero Recycling, 20 Microns, Lohum Magnets & Energy Solutions, NEO Performance Materials of Singapore and Proterial India responded. “Twenty companies and consortia submitted bids, bringing together established engineering companies, public-sector enterprises, recycling specialists, energy companies, magnet manufacturers and international participants,” the publication said. The scheme targets up to five beneficiaries, selected through global competitive bidding, each eligible for as much as 1,200 metric tonnes per annum. The scheme design places production at the centre of the programme, the report said, adding that it connects government support to the actual manufacture and sale of magnets rather than focusing solely on creating facilities. The publication mentioned broad participation of firms from different industrial backgrounds as evidence of rare-earth processing and magnet manufacturing being viewed as a wider industrial opportunity. India’s policy emphasis is now shifting towards connecting substantial rare-earth resources with industrial value chains. Government assessments indicated a huge gap between upstream capabilities and industrial-scale midstream and downstream manufacturing. The timing of the rare-earth push is also closely connected to India’s broader technology and manufacturing ambitions along with advances in mobile phones and electronics exports, Permanent magnets sit at the intersection of many of these sectors including semiconductors, electric mobility, renewable energy equipment and advanced manufacturing. bihar_raw_news.title: Rahul Gandhi backs Bihar students, warns BJP over youth protests | Daily Pioneer
bihar_raw_news.content: September 03, 2026 Rahul Gandhi backs Bihar students, warns BJP against suppressing voice of youth Copy Link X WhatsApp Share By Pioneer News Service Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi interacts with students from Bihar injured during protests against alleged irregularities in examination system, at his residence, in New Delhi. (@RahulGandhi/X via PTI Photo) Congress leader and Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi on Thursday backed students and youngsters in Bihar who protested against alleged irregularities in the examination system, and warned the BJP that any government that suppresses the voice of the youth will eventually have to answer to the people. Gandhi made the remarks after meeting students and young people who, he said, had faced “horrific police brutality” while raising their concerns over the examination system. “Police lathis as well as gunfire from AK-47 and pistols left many students injured. A young man aspiring to serve the country in the Army had his leg battered by an AK-47 bullet -- and with it, his life-long dream was also shattered,” Gandhi said in a post in Hindi on X. He said the protesters were only demanding fair opportunities, a transparent examination system and their rights. “What was the need to use lathis and bullets in response to such demands?” Gandhi asked. He also rejected any attempt to hold only lower-ranking officials responsible for the police action. “The government cannot absolve itself of responsibility for such extreme brutality by merely blaming a few low-ranking officials. This action is either the result of orders from above or a sign of the administration's utter failure,” he said. Gandhi said he stood with the protesting youngsters and was ready to provide them with all possible assistance. “The BJP should remember: any regime that suppresses the voice of the youth eventually has to answer to the people. That day is not far off,” he said. Patna witnessed clashes between job aspirants and police last month after protesters tried to march towards the chief minister’s residence, demanding a single-tier teacher recruitment examination and a transparent recruitment process. The students’ agitation, which began in the first week of August, has received support from opposition leaders, including RJD working president Tejashwi Yadav. 0 Likes 0 Dislikes Bookmark 0 Comments Leave a Comment

bihar_raw_news.title: Foodgrain production estimated at 376.5 million tonnes amid robust decentralised grain storage infra
bihar_raw_news.content: Business 03 Sep, 2026 Foodgrain production estimated at 376.5 million tonnes amid robust decentralised grain storage infra Business To Business, New Delhi, 03 September 2026: The country’s total foodgrain production is estimated at 376.563 million tonnes, according to the Third Advance Estimates (2025-26), which is nearly 18.8 million tonnes (5.3 per cent) higher than last year’s production of 357.732 million tonnes, an official factsheet said on Thursday. India also operates one of the world’s largest food security programmes under the National Food Security Act, 2013, that covers about 80 crore people. “India’s expanding agricultural production and food security efforts have increased the importance of decentralised grain storage infrastructure across the country. The Decentralised Grain Storage Plan in Cooperative Sector, launched in 2023, is designed to improve storage, processing, procurement, and distribution systems through Primary Agricultural Credit Societies (PACS),” the factsheet noted. The plan is supported through institutional coordination and financial support mechanisms. Beginning with pilot projects across 11 states/PACS with 9,750 MT of storage capacity, the initiative has expanded steadily. As of July 2026, godown construction had been completed in 313 PACS across the country, creating more than 1.80 LMT of storage capacity. The framework also emphasises quality standards, transparency and operational viability, according to the factsheet. The Decentralised Grain Storage Plan in Cooperative Sector seeks to reduce foodgrain wastage and strengthen food security; provide farmers with greater flexibility to avoid distress sales and secure better price realization; reduce transportation costs between procurement centres, warehouses, and Fair Price Shops; and expand the role of Primary Agricultural Credit Societies (PACS) through diversification of agricultural activities. It also supports higher income opportunities for farmers. The pilot projects were implemented in Maharashtra, Uttar Pradesh, Gujarat, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Tamil Nadu, Telangana, Assam, Karnataka, and Tripura. These pilots have provided an important operational foundation and demonstrated the feasibility of local storage infrastructure at the cooperative level, said the factsheet. According to the official statement, the Decentralised Grain Storage Plan in Cooperative Sector represents an integrated approach towards improving agricultural infrastructure through cooperatives. By linking storage, processing, procurement, and distribution at the PACS level, the Plan strengthens foodgrain management closer to production centres. national_raw_news.content: India has announced the decision to appoint a Defence Attache to Brussels, complementing Belgium placing a Defence Attache in New Delhi earlier this year. Briefing media this evening on Belgian Prime Minister, Bart De Wever’s visit, Secretary (West) in External Affairs Ministry, Sibi George affirmed that significant progress will be seen in defence engagement between the two nations, including in defence production. He said that Prime Minister Narendra Modi and the Belgian Prime Minister have set a target to double bilateral trade in the next five years in the backdrop of successful conclusion of India-EU FTA. Currently the trade is about 13 billion US dollars. Secretary (West) emphasised that there is a clear focus on three Ts – Trade, Technology and Talent. Prime Minister Modi has invited the Belgian universities and premier academic institutions to open campuses in India. Mr George said that Prime Minister Modi also invited Belgium to participate in the WAVES 2.0. On whether views regarding Russia-Ukraine and West Asia conflicts were exchanged between the two leaders, Secretary (West) informed that both sides exchanged views on major international developments, including the recent developments in Ukraine and West Asia. Regarding Ukraine, both sides reaffirmed support for efforts towards the achievement of a comprehensive, just, and lasting peace through dialogue and diplomacy. On West Asia, they discussed the recent developments in the region and underscored the importance of dialogue and diplomatic engagement to address challenges in a peaceful manner. Replying to a query on the extradition of fugitive Mehul Choksi, Mr George said that the fugitive was arrested by the Belgian authorities in April last year, and has been in Belgian jail since then. He said Indian government remains committed to ensuring that fugitives are brought back to India to face law and justice.

national_raw_news.title: 2 hours ago | National 60 EAM S Jaishankar expresses India’s support in any manner possible to end Russia- Ukraine war
national_raw_news.content: External Affairs Minister Dr S Jaishankar today said that India has consistently maintained that this is not an era of war, and that solutions will not emerge from the battlefield. The Minister said this after meeting his Ukrainian counterpart Andrii Sybiha in Kyiv, Ukraine. Dr Jaishankar reiterated Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s statement just two days ago in Bishkek, that endless war must now give way to the end of war. He said that every passing day of conflict only means more deaths and more destruction. The Minister also expressed country’s support in any manner possible to end Ukraine’s ongoing conflict with Russia. Dr Jaishankar also highlighted attacks on commercial shipping during such conflicts, and said that it impacts many nations of the Global South in a variety of ways leading to fuel, fertilizer and food shortages. He said that India has so far provided 19 consignments of humanitarian assistance to Ukraine, including 160 tonnes comprising generator sets, medicines, and medical equipment. He said that the two countries have a considerable history and it predates Ukraine’s independence. Dr Jaishankar stressed that trade between India and Ukraine spans across many sectors including pharmaceuticals, food, agriculture and fertilizers. Noting future prospects of their bilateral cooperation, the Minister said that the two countries are progressing in areas of digital capabilities, innovation and startups. He further said, the world of AI In a social media post, the Minister said that he discussed ways to further strengthen bilateral relationship, including in the fields of education, health, agriculture, digital, innovation, diplomatic training and development cooperation with his Ukrainian counterpart. During the meeting, Dr Jaishankar was updated on the recent developments in the ongoing conflict and peace negotiations. He also conveyed the need to ensure the safety and security of commercial shipping and seafarers. Later, Dr Jaishankar also met Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy and discussed on approaches to end the ongoing conflict. The Minister is on a three-day visit to Ukraine and Poland.

national_raw_news.title: 2 hours ago | International 115 Kyiv welcomes PM Modi’s call to end ongoing conflict with Russia: Ukraine FM Andrii Sybiha
national_raw_news.content: Describing India as a global power, Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha today said his country welcomes Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s call to end the ongoing conflict between Ukrain and Russia. Ukraine stands ready for diplomacy, Sybiha said in a social media post as he met External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar, who arrived Kyiv to hold bilateral consultations with his Ukrainian counterpart amid escalating hostilities between Moscow and Kyiv. Jaishankar’s visit to Kyiv comes amid concerns in New Delhi over the killing of an Indian in the Ukrainian capital this week following a Russian strike. In his social media post, Sybiha welcomed Jaishankar to Kyiv terming it the first-ever dedicated bilateral visit of an Indian External Affairs Minister to Ukraine. He said that the two sides discussed the need to restore freedom of navigation in the Black Sea and global food security. India has been concerned over a series of attacks on merchant ships in the Black Sea in the last few weeks. Sybiha said the two sides also discussed bilateral cooperation, from infrastructure and the pharmaceutical sector to technological innovation and digitalisation. He said both countries are ready to realise their full potential. At a meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin in Bishkek on the margins of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation summit earlier this week, Prime Minister Modi called for ending the conflict through diplomacy and dialogue. In August 2024, Prime Minister Modi visited the Ukrainian capital city of Kyiv and conveyed to President Volodymyr Zelenskyy that both Ukraine and Russia should sit together without wasting time to end the war. India has been consistently calling for ending the Russia-Ukraine conflict through dialogue and diplomacy.

national_raw_news.title: 4 hours ago | National 113 India, Belgium reaffirm their commitment to deepening trade, investment and economic cooperation
national_raw_news.content: India and Belgium today reaffirmed their commitment to deepening trade, investment and economic cooperation. Prime Minister Narendra Modi and the Prime Minister of Belgium, Bart De Wever welcomed the growing diversification of sectors in bilateral trade in the India-Belgium Joint Statement released after the talks between the two leaders. India and Belgium have set an ambitious goal of doubling bilateral trade over the next five years. The two sides identified significant potential for cooperation in pharmaceuticals, life sciences, semiconductors, defence manufacturing, critical minerals, renewable energy, ports, logistics, space and advanced technologies. With Belgium as the 24th biggest economy in the world, and India’s ambition to become a 10 trillion dollar economy in the coming years, both leaders acknowledged abundant opportunities for mutually beneficial partnerships. Both leaders also welcomed the successful conclusion of negotiations on the India-EU Free Trade Agreement and called for its timely implementation. They also called for early completion of negotiations on the India-EU Investment Protection Agreement and the Geographical Indications Agreement. On defence and security, Belgium conveyed solidarity with India in the fight against terrorism and condemned the terror attack in Pahalgam. Both sides agreed to strengthen cooperation against terrorism and explore the establishment of a Joint Working Group on Counter-Terrorism. The two countries also signed a Letter of Intent to strengthen defence cooperation through regular exchanges, training, research and defence-industrial partnerships. A Memorandum of Understanding was also signed between the Central Bureau of Investigation and the Federal Police of Belgium to combat transnational organised crime and cybercrime. Prime Minister Modi and visiting Prime Minister Wever welcomed the launch of the India-Belgium Strategic Dialogue. They also stressed the need for reform of the United Nations Security Council. Belgium reaffirmed its support for India’s candidature for permanent membership of a reformed and expanded Security Council. India and Belgium renewed their cooperation in renewable energy, including green hydrogen, solar power, energy storage and offshore wind. The leaders also encouraged greater cooperation in semiconductors, artificial intelligence, startups and emerging technologies. The two sides agreed to strengthen connectivity and people-to-people ties by expanding visa processing capacity and exploring direct air connectivity between India and Belgium. Prime Minister Modi also invited leading Belgian universities to establish campuses in India. The two leaders exchanged views on international issues, including the situations in Ukraine and West Asia, and reaffirmed their support for dialogue and diplomacy to address conflicts. Belgian Prime Minister Wever invited Prime Minister Modi to visit Belgium at a mutually convenient time. The two leaders reaffirmed their commitment to further deepening the India-Belgium partnership, guided by mutual trust, democracy, the rule of law and a shared vision of peace, prosperity and development.

national_raw_news.title: Union Minister of Commerce & Industry Shri Piyush Goyal Calls for Nationwide FTA ... - PIB
national_raw_news.content: Ministry of Commerce & Industry Union Minister of Commerce & Industry Shri Piyush Goyal Calls for Nationwide FTA Utilisation Drive to Expand India’s Global Trade Footprint India’s nine FTAs spanning economies with about $60 trillion GDP to provide preferential access to nearly two-thirds of global trade: Shri Goyal Combined with upcoming FTAs and efforts to deepen market access, India could gain access to 75% of global trade at rates lower than competitors India’s exports reach about $317 billion during April-July, up by $36-37 billion over corresponding period last year Calls for FTA outreach to reach every district, MSME, trader, entrepreneur, startup and woman entrepreneur Posted On: 03 SEP 2026 1:56PM by PIB Delhi Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Shri Piyush Goyal today called for a focused, inclusive and nationwide effort to maximise the utilisation of Free Trade Agreements (FTAs) to expand India’s trade across the world and ensure that the benefits of enhanced market access reach businesses across the country. Addressing the National Workshop on “Leveraging FTAs an Outreach Programme” in New Delhi today, Shri Goyal emphasised the need for a concerted effort to translate India’s expanding network of FTAs into greater export opportunities for businesses across the country. Shri Goyal said the initiative should rapidly take roots across the country and reach the last person, smallest business person, trader, entrepreneur, startup and woman entrepreneur across all 780 districts, big and small. He said every contribution, big or small, would be invaluable in achieving the larger objective of transforming India from a largely inward-looking domestic economy into an international player of significance. The day-long workshop brought together senior officials from the Central Government, States and Union Territories, Export Promotion Councils and industry associations, with the objective of translating India’s expanding network of Free Trade Agreements into measurable outcomes for Indian exporters, particularly MSMEs and first-time exporters. The Minister said India should become an economy recognised and respected across the world for its contributions and a trusted partner of the world. He said this trust should translate into value and that this value proposition should emerge from collective efforts across the country towards making India a $30 trillion economy by 2047, with a very large share of international trade. Shri Goyal said India was passing through an important phase of its economic journey and highlighted the first-quarter GDP growth of 7.8% at constant prices. He said achieving 7.8% GDP growth amid uncertainty and tremendous turmoil around the world was a significant achievement. He urged people not to be guided by the “naysayers”. The Minister said the GDP numbers were not made by the government, ministers or bureaucrats, but were determined through an elaborate, ground-up and independent process run by the Ministry of Statistics, which has been in place for decades. The Minister called for continued, consistent, relentless and outcome-oriented efforts, with greater inclusion to take the entire country along, encourage new entrepreneurs to look at global markets and utilise the tremendous opportunities that have opened up.
